JEMBER REGENCY GOVERNMENT

JEMBER REGENCY REGIONAL REGULATION

NUMBER 4 OF 2008

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF JEMBER,

Considering:
a. that in order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Jember Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence in Jember Regency; b. that in order for the handling of violence against women and children in Jember Regency to be carried out more effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence in Jember Regency; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Jember Regency. In View of:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

6 -

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.
27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives.

Article 9

1. The community is obligated to make efforts to provide support for the development of violence prevention programs (2) The community is obligated to prepare proposals regarding the formulation and policies on protection (3) The community is obligated to make efforts to protect and provide moral or material support to victims (4) The community is obligated to conduct supervision and reporting of acts of violence to the competent authorities.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES

Article 2

The principles of protection of women and children victims of violence are:
1. Respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims
2. Justice and gender equality

3. Non-discrimination
4. Best interests of victims

CHAPTER IX

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 17

1. Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the laws and regulations.
2. Appointed officials who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
3. Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
4. Administrative actions and or sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be imposed in accordance with the laws and regulations.

12 - (5) PPT managers who carry out service duties and violate service principles shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is action based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men. Domestic realm means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public realm means the space where relations concerning public interests occur. Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about gender-based violence.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 16

1. Guidance on the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by related Agencies in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that include technical implementation of protection for Women and Children.
3. Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by related agencies together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Number 1 Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

1 - - 2 - Number 2 Gender justice is a condition where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3 Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4 The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Obtain protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels.
2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers.

7 -

3. Obtain integrated services in accordance with service principles.
4. Make legal claims and or lawsuits through judicial bodies and or courts outside the court, and may report to the International Court
5. Obtain information about laws and regulations that protect victims
6. Obtain confidential handling
7. Obtain information and be involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.
8. Obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother or child, family member, household member, and community member.
9. Obtain accompaniment at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
10. Obtain continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
11. Obtain protection from identity disclosure through mass media.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 12

The forms of services for victims organized by P3A include:

1. Medical services, in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
2. Medicolegal services are a form of medical service for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
3. Psychosocial services are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide social support so that victims have self-confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems.
4. Legal services are services to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
5. Economic independence services in the form of services for skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

6. Information Services (Informed Consent), related to services and assistance

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) Social workers are persons who provide social services to women and children victims of violence who understand service principles

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
2. The Regency Integrated Service Center receives case referrals from service institutions in the Regency area.
3. Provisions regarding the Integrated Service Center will be regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3

Article 2

1. Respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims
2. Justice and gender equality

3. Non-discrimination
4. Best interests of victims

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.

Article 3

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and or public sphere.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

THE REGENT OF JEMBER

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN  AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

6 -

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.
27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives.

3. Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
4. Administrative actions and or sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be imposed in accordance with the laws and regulations.

12 - (5) PPT managers who carry out service duties and violate service principles shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 8

The Management of Women and Children Protection implemented by the Integrated Service Center has the obligation to organize services in accordance with the service principles as regulated in the Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

6 -

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.
27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Obtain protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels.
2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers.

7 -

3. Obtain integrated services in accordance with service principles.
4. Make legal claims and or lawsuits through judicial bodies and or courts outside the court, and may report to the International Court
5. Obtain information about laws and regulations that protect victims
6. Obtain confidential handling
7. Obtain information and be involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.
8. Obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother or child, family member, household member, and community member.
9. Obtain accompaniment at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
10. Obtain continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
11. Obtain protection from identity disclosure through mass media.

Article 10

2. The Regency Integrated Service Center receives case referrals from service institutions in the Regency area.
3. Provisions regarding the Integrated Service Center will be regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 2

Number 1 Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

1 - - 2 - Number 2 Gender justice is a condition where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Number 3 Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Number 4 The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER IX

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 17

1. Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the laws and regulations.
2. Appointed officials who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
3. Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
4. Administrative actions and or sanctions as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be imposed in accordance with the laws and regulations.

12 - (5) PPT managers who carry out service duties and violate service principles shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is action based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men. Domestic realm means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public realm means the space where relations concerning public interests occur. Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about gender-based violence.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 16

3. Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by related agencies together with the Government's internal supervisory apparatus in accordance with Laws and Regulations.

Article 12

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.

13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. 18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.

20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 9

1. The community is obligated to make efforts to provide support for the development of violence prevention programs (2) The community is obligated to prepare proposals regarding the formulation and policies on protection (3) The community is obligated to make efforts to protect and provide moral or material support to victims (4) The community is obligated to conduct supervision and reporting of acts of violence to the competent authorities.

9 -

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is action based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men. Domestic realm means the space where interpersonal relations occur; public realm means the space where relations concerning public interests occur. Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about gender-based violence.

2. Appointed officials who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.
3. Appointed officials who fail to carry out supervision as stipulated in Article 15 shall be subject to administrative actions and or sanctions.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Obtain protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels.
2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers.

7 -

3. Obtain integrated services in accordance with service principles.
4. Make legal claims and or lawsuits through judicial bodies and or courts outside the court, and may report to the International Court
5. Obtain information about laws and regulations that protect victims
6. Obtain confidential handling
7. Obtain information and be involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.
8. Obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother or child, family member, household member, and community member.
9. Obtain accompaniment at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
10. Obtain continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
11. Obtain protection from identity disclosure through mass media.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Article 3

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and or public sphere.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

6 -

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and or public sphere.

PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES AND SERVICE PRINCIPLES

4. Best interests of victims

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF VICTIMS

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Obtain protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels.
2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers.

3. Obtain integrated services in accordance with service principles.
4. Make legal claims and or lawsuits through judicial bodies and or courts outside the court, and may report to the International Court
5. Obtain information about laws and regulations that protect victims
6. Obtain confidential handling
7. Obtain information and be involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.
8. Obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother or child, family member, household member, and community member.
9. Obtain accompaniment at every level of examination and during the judicial process.
10. Obtain continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.
11. Obtain protection from identity disclosure through mass media.
