CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

14. 17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.
27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The State has an obligation to provide security to its citizens from threats and actions that may disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual or economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1948 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XA of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a fair and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration
2. Regent is the Regent of Jember
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb
4. Woman is a person of female gender
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim
6. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life
7. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
8. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death.
9. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
10. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse - 5 - in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred
13. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination
14. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.

Article 5

Every victim has the right to:

1. Obtain protection from the community and government as well as non-governmental institutions at the local, national and international levels.
2. Obtain information about the location of complaint centers.

17. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedure regulated by law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court hearing.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him or her in a civil manner
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operational Procedure hereinafter referred to as SOP is a standard operational procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.

23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBD is the APBD of Jember Regency.
27. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBN is the annual financial plan of the State Government approved by the House of Representatives.

JEMBER REGENCY GOVERNMENT

JEMBER REGENCY REGIONAL REGULATION

NUMBER 4 OF 2008

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN JEMBER REGENCY

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF JEMBER,

Considering:
a. that in order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Jember Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence in Jember Regency; b. that in order for the handling of violence against women and children in Jember Regency to be carried out more effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence in Jember Regency; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Jember Regency.
